Fixed in PR #88 (superseded PR #86). Root cause: requestAuthorization fired correctly, but for an LSUIElement app macOS presents the prompt as an ordinary corner banner with Allow revealed only on hover - no modal, no dock bounce. Left unanswered and then quit, macOS records the answer as PERMANENTLY denied, after which requestAuthorization returns UNErrorDomain code 1 immediately and add() silently no-ops. The old { _, _ in } callback discarded both the grant and the error, so the dead end left no trace. Ruled out empirically with throwaway bundle ids: the App.init() call site, LSUIElement blocking presentation, needing to be frontmost, and the app being quit before the callback completed. Fix: ReminderAuthorization value type + NotificationAuthorizer protocol mirroring LoginItemSetting/LoginItemRegistrar; the popover renders the problem with an Open Notification Settings button and refreshes on .task so granting clears it without a relaunch. Verified on a fresh bundle id: prompt presented AND app listed in System Settings.

Implemented across PR #87 (demolition) and PR #88 (construction). ThrowntomAlert target, the Go alert plumbing, findAlertHelper and the darwinNotifier alert methods are gone; the Notifier interface is back to PlaySound only. The macOS app now posts the reminder itself on awaiting_confirm via a pure ReminderBanner.decide(from:to:authorization:) over two daemon states, with a thin ReminderPresenter adapter, and answers Snooze/Confirm in-process through the same DaemonClient path as every other button. Verified on-device: one banner across 32s of continuous awaiting_confirm frames, Snooze produced a snoozed event in the daemon log, Confirm advanced awaiting_confirm to short_break, and both leaving the phase and quitting the app withdrew the banner. KNOWN GAP: throwntom-ux2 - the cycle snooze publishes no state change, so a snooze that expires resumes the sound with no banner. Cause is upstream in handleSnooze/App.Snooze; decide() already handles a non-nil snooze_until correctly.

Resolved by throwntom-0ej (PRs #87, #88) per ADR-003. The buttons now work: the macOS app posts the notification itself, so the process holding it is the one that stays alive and can answer. Verified on-device 2026-08-27 - clicking Snooze produced a snoozed event in the daemon log and clicking Confirm advanced awaiting_confirm to short_break, where before neither reached the daemon at all. Note for the record: this bead's original evidence criterion (snooze_until stayed null) was the wrong field - snooze_until is only ever set by the morning path, so it would have been null here even had the button worked. See throwntom-ux2, which tracks the separate remaining gap that a cycle snooze publishes no state change and so no banner returns when it expires.

Fixed on fix/readme-image-transparency (79a445e, c1b5d38, e292319).

Root cause: docs/images/throwntom.png was 512x512 8-bit RGB, hasAlpha: no, exported over an off-white (254,254,254) backdrop - not pure white, which is why a naive un-matte left corners at alpha 1.

Could NOT reuse macos/mask-icon.swift as the bead suggested: the README banner is DIFFERENT artwork from the app icon (badge + wordmark vs plain tomato), so that pipeline would have replaced the art. Its edge is also a soft ~20px glow, not a geometric shape - fitting a continuous rounded rect bottomed out at ~5px RMSE, so any squircle mask would clip art or leave white slivers.

Fix: new tools/unmatte-white-background.swift recovers alpha by flood-filling the backdrop inward from the four corners (white INSIDE the art - badge ring, wordmark - is enclosed by opaque pixels and never reached) and un-compositing each background pixel from the backdrop colour sampled at a seeding corner. Original art preserved as docs/images/throwntom-source.png; the banner is generated from it and regeneration is byte-stable (sha256 8255078d). Documented in docs/development.md and README.

Result: hasAlpha yes, 512x512 unchanged, all four corners alpha=0, 0 artwork pixels changed, composite over the backdrop reproduces the source within 1/255. Verified over both white and dark (#0d1117).

Two review rounds hardened the --verify guard, which mattered more than the asset: as first written it asserted only four corner pixels and passed a file with the whole surround still opaque; it also silently weakened to a tolerance-2 RGB check, and re-running the fill validated a mask against itself so a leaked mask passed. Now: exact byte equality for artwork, whole-surround assertion, refusal when no corner seeds the fill, and --max-surround (default 25%) to catch a leaked --threshold (banner claims 4.6%; threshold 30 leaks to 49.7% and is now a hard error).

DECISION: sound_command stays startup-only; the docs were wrong and are fixed instead (dfdeb2a). Reason: throwntomd never reads cfg.SoundCommand at all. The only non-test read is cmd/throwntom/startup.go:91 (tuiNotifier), and cmd/throwntomd/main.go:67-69 injects notifier.Silent() per ADR-007, whose PlaySound returns nil without playing (internal/notifier/notifier.go:65). Making it reloadable would reload a value the daemon has no use for. The template previously claimed 'A change here waits for the daemon to restart', which is false in the other direction too: restarting throwntomd does not make sound_command take effect, because the daemon plays nothing either way. internal/config/template.go now documents it as a throwntom terminal-interface setting that the TUI reads once as it launches. Secondary point, recorded but not relied on: keeping it startup-only also means a config write cannot introduce new subprocess execution into a running process — though the TUI has no reload path at all, so there is nothing there to exploit; the 'daemon has no use for it' argument carries the decision on its own. No code change.

Root cause: launch-agent registration is destructive, not idempotent. AgentRegistrationPlan.steps(for: .enabled) is [.unregister, .register] and the unregister boots out a running launchd job; DaemonClient re-registered on every 3rd consecutive failure, and 'outage' means 'no decodable frame yet', not 'daemon not running'. With the default backoff, ask #1 lands ~1.5s and ask #2 ~9s - on a daemon that started ~8s in and is still inside launchd's default 10s minimum runtime (plist has KeepAlive, no ThrottleInterval), so launchd throttles the respawn. That is the mechanism behind throwntom-mwh's '8s steps that do not help'. Fix: ReconnectBackoff.registerAgentIfDue(_:) makes at most ONE ACCEPTED registration per outage; a refused ask fixed nothing so it is retried at the next multiple. Safe because after an accepted ask launchd's KeepAlive is the retry mechanism and re-asking can only interrupt it. Proved with three tests that fail against the old code (registrar called 3x, expected 1). Branch fix/transport-registration, not pushed. Follow-up throwntom-azp filed for the window saying 'Starting timer…' forever after an accepted ask that never yields a daemon.

shouldRegisterAgent + agentRegistered() replaced by one mutating func registerAgentIfDue(_ register: () -> Bool) that decides, asks, checks acceptance, rewinds and sets the once-flag as one indivisible call. hasAskedLaunchdToStart is now private, so no caller can read half the protocol and silently lose the rewind. Delivered together with throwntom-svm, whose fix needed the same seam: the 'once' the flag guarded turned out to be load-bearing for correctness, not just for the rewind. Doc comment now also states that the closure must not touch the backoff (mutating call holds exclusive access).

waitUntil now takes a required description and defaults file/line to the call site; on giving up it calls XCTFail(file:line:) so the failure lands on the waiting line, then throws a TimeoutError whose description names the condition, the timeout and the call site. A cancelled sleep - what an overrunning MainActor test produces - is caught and reported as that same named wait instead of propagating a bare CancellationError. New pollUntil seam returns the failure rather than reporting it, so the helper's own behaviour is testable without XCTest swallowing the assertions under test (XCTExpectFailure was tried first and absorbed them, making the tests unfailable). All 33 call sites named.

The retry is bfz's own Start control, not a second affordance - and startService() now drops the parked reconnect loop so pressing it dials immediately instead of waiting out up to 8s of backoff. Prose-only, and does not undermine the fix. The arithmetic in a rationale note inside the interaction log may be off (9s vs ~15.5s for when the second registration ask lands), but throwntom-svm's fix does not rest on that number: it was proven by a test that FAILS against the old code (testTheAgentIsRegisteredOnlyOncePerOutage, 3 registrations vs 1), and re-verified by deleting the guard and watching three tests fail. The mechanism — registration is destructive (unregister+register) and can boot out a daemon inside launchd's 10s minimum runtime — holds regardless of exactly when the ask lands. Correcting a number in an append-only log is not worth a code change.

Fixed on fix/flaky-e2e-resize (0638f3c, f4a602e, bfdcdbc, 3bbd176). Fixed on feature/snooze-lifecycle (fc6794a..0726706, not pushed). New 'unsnooze' command + POST /v1/timer/unsnooze, backed by outstandingReminder.unsuppress() which shares endSuppressionLocked() with the deadline-driven resume(). SEMANTICS: cancelling re-raises the reminder AT ONCE, because ADR-004 defines snooze_until as 'the deadline the outstanding reminder is suppressed until' - the reminder is suppressed, never answered - so ending it early must land exactly where letting it expire lands. reminder.Loop.Run alerts before its first ticker wait, so the nudge is immediate. Refused with 409 'nothing to unsnooze: no snooze is active' when no snooze is running. BEAD PREMISE WAS PARTLY WRONG (see notes): start and skip-today ALREADY cleared a snooze via reminder.cancel(); what was missing was a non-committal way out, since both RETIRE the reminder rather than ending the suppression, and start additionally forces a work period. The bead's 'stop is the LOSSY verb' line was also stale - throwntom-k08 closed with stop as a suspend. ALSO FIXED, mentioned by neither bead: an active snooze was completely invisible. Snoozing withdraws the reminder banner (ReminderBanner.waitingKind), so nothing on screen showed it. MainWindowContent.snoozeNote now prints 'Snoozed · MM:SS left' and the Snooze chip becomes 'Cancel Snooze' while one runs, so the undo sits on the control that caused it. Tooling path the bead asked for: 'tomctl cmd unsnooze'. Chime interaction verified by test, not assumed: suppress() stops the ring loop so reminder_rings stops climbing and the client stops chiming (ADR-007), and unsnooze restarts it without resetting the count, so heard rings are not replayed. Deferred: throwntom-jyi, a pre-existing stray-ring race this made easier to hit.

DECIDED (Joe, 2026-08-30): keep client presentation preferences in config.toml. In his words, it is 'a better user experience to have a single place to put configs such as config.toml'. So float_window_when_waiting staying in the shared config, parsed by Go and published in core.State, is correct and no change is needed. This settles the general question, not just this key: macOS-only preferences belong in config.toml alongside everything else, not in UserDefaults or an app-private store. Consistent with throwntom-plg, which made the fully-commented config.toml the settings experience (the app's Open Config File… ⌘, is the settings UI for now). ADR-003 still governs who OWNS presentation — the client decides what to do — but where the user TYPES the preference is a config-UX question, and one file wins.

PREMISE STILL TRUE on current main (644f524). Reproduced deterministically: with the guard removed, an alert arriving from a cancelled loop raises the published ring count (2 -> 3).

DECISION: quietLocked must NOT ack, and the loop's early-ack check is NOT wrong. They are different verbs. Ack means the reminder was ANSWERED, so it rightly stops even the first alert. Cancelling ctx means this loop is RETIRED, which is not an answer -- and none of quietLocked's four callers means 'answered': raise and endSuppressionLocked retire a loop only to start its replacement, and suppress explicitly must not claim an answer, because a snooze silences a reminder that was never answered (ADR-004; internal/core/outstanding.go:129-133). Acking there asserted an answer nobody gave, which is why it swallowed the first ring.

FIX, placed with the one owner (ADR-004): the loop's own ctx is its identity. loopNotify(ctx) carries it, and ring(loop, promised) tests loop.Err() inside the same critical section that raises the count. quietLocked cancels while holding mu, so an alert that finds ctx live got there before the cancel -- the ordering is decided, not raced. The loop's FIRST alert is exempt: a raise promises one ring, and whether the user hears it must not depend on goroutine scheduling. internal/reminder/loop.go is unchanged apart from doc comments recording the ack-vs-cancel distinction.

Tests: TestAnAlertFromARetiredLoopDoesNotRaiseTheCount (discriminator -- fails without the guard) and TestThePromisedFirstAlertSurvivesARetirementThatBeatsIt (the pin -- fails if the guard is made unconditional, i.e. the exact 6->5 regression class). TestSilentNotifierStillDrivesReminderState still sees 6.

Decisions the bead asked for: transient dialling announces NOTHING in either direction, so a socket blip is never a spoken interruption. Because every recovery passes through dialling, the announcer measures against the last SETTLED situation rather than the previous one -- a blip returns to what it left and stays silent, a Start the user pressed does not and says 'Timer service running.' The window never announces its own launch. Wording is the screen's own title plus its own sentence, so a VoiceOver and a sighted user get the same words; the refused screen speaks its title alone, because its sentence comes from launchd via the client rather than from the situation. All of it is written up in DESIGN.md's 'Screens without a timer service (macOS)' section, as the bead suggested.

Code: ServiceStatus.announcement(from:to:) for wording, ServiceAnnouncer for the memory, posted from MainWindow via AccessibilityNotification.Announcement at .high priority so it interrupts rather than being dropped mid-utterance.

Tests cover the wording and the sequence thoroughly (ServiceStatusTests: cold start, blip, prolonged dial, recovery from each of the three absences, repeats, distinctness). Added while verifying: testTheSpokenLineIsTheWindowsOwnTitle, which asserts the spoken line really is the window's ConnectionStatus title rather than a second literal that could drift from it.

VERIFICATION LIMIT -- NOT PROVEN: no test here demonstrates that VoiceOver actually speaks. A test process with no app bundle cannot. Worse, the wiring itself is untested: deleting the whole .onChange in MainWindow that drives the announcement leaves the entire suite green (measured). So what is proven is that the announcer computes the right strings and silences; what is NOT proven is that the window ever calls it, or that anything is spoken. Filed as throwntom-9w9. Manual verification with VoiceOver on has not been done.
